proposal.summary: WinGate 9.4.1.5998 installation directory has insecure permissions allowing authenticated local users to replace WinGate.exe and achieve code execution as SYSTEM after a service restart or system reboot.
proposal.cwe_quote:
WinGate has insecure permissions for the installation directory, which allows local
users ability to gain privileges by replacing an executable file with a Trojan horse.

PR.quote:
The WinGate directory hands (F) full control to authenticated users, who can then run
arbitrary code as SYSTEM after a WinGate restart or system reboot.

UI.quote: Logon as standard user replace WinGate.exe with a trojan executable, wait for restart or reboot the system, your code runs as SYSTEM.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify file-system ACLs on the WinGate installation directory and remove write/modify/replace permissions from Authenticated Users; consider notifying vendor for patched release and publish a vendor advisory describing secure permissions and mitigation steps.

evidence_quotes.claim: Permissions allow replacement of executable leading to SYSTEM code execution
evidence_quotes.quote:
WinGate has insecure permissions for the installation directory, which allows local
users ability to gain privileges by replacing an executable file with a Trojan horse.

evidence_quotes.claim: Directory ACL showing Authenticated Users have Full control
evidence_quotes.quote:
C:\Program Files\WinGate>cacls WinGate.exe
C:\Program Files\WinGate\WinGate.exe NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users:(ID)F
                                     NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(ID)F
                                     BUILTIN\Administrators:(ID)F
                                     BUILTIN\Users:(ID)R
                                     APPLICATION PACKAGE AUTHORITY\ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES:(ID)R
                                     APPLICATION PACKAGE AUTHORITY\ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES:(ID)R
Logon as standard user replace WinGate.exe with a trojan executable, wait for restart or reboot the system, your code runs as SYSTEM.
